adapters.productionRole: Generate OCDS packages outside the deployed Worker, then import them through the STS normalization and provenance boundary.

findings: The source package has broad parser and transformer tests that pass at the audited commit.
The scheduled refresh workflow fails during uv setup because it enables caching without a checked-in uv.lock.
The workflow invokes opencontractsau while pyproject.toml declares the opencontractau console script.
Package metadata declares 0.15.0 while opencontractau.__version__ reports 0.13.1.
Incremental since filtering is supported only for ACT, NSW_LIVE and AUSTENDER; other adapters silently ignore it.
Scraper-level network, parsing and blocking exceptions propagate to the caller and require adapter-level retry and quarantine handling.
Coverage is useful but partial; SA, statewide WA and QTenders remain gaps or deferred paths.
The repository publishes code, not a guaranteed bulk corpus or service-level agreement.

controls: Identify the audited source by commit SHA, not runtime __version__.
Prefer official AusTender and NSW feeds when records overlap.
Validate every package as an OCDS release package before import.
Retain package URI, upstream commit, source metadata and license in provenance.
Maintain a per-jurisdiction cursor strategy instead of assuming since is honoured.
Treat silently ignored date filters as unsupported.
Apply timeouts, bounded retries and quarantine outside the upstream package.
Record collection window and record count for every jurisdiction run.
Do not rely on upstream scheduled refreshes until their workflow is passing.
